questions.question: Mohenjodaro site of Harappan civilisation is situated on the bank of which river?
questions.solution: Mohenjodaro (meaning 'Mound of the Dead') is located on the bank of the Indus River in the Larkana district of Sindh, Pakistan. Discovery: Found by R.D. Banerji in 1922.

questions.question: Who was/were the founder(s) of the Theosophical Society?
questions.option_2: H P Blavatsky and Colonel Olcott
questions.option_4: Charles W Leadbeater and Emily Lutyens
questions.solution: The Theosophical Society was founded in 1875 in New York by Madame H.P. Blavatsky and Colonel M.S. Olcott. In India: They shifted their headquarters to Adyar (Madras) in 1882. Annie Besant became its president later.

questions.question: Who among the following leaders founded the women’s wing of Congress in 1940?
questions.solution: Sucheta Kriplani founded the All India Mahila Congress (Women's wing of INC) in 1940. Achievement: She later became the first woman Chief Minister of an Indian state (Uttar Pradesh).

questions.question: Who among the following was the Vice President of the Interim Government formed by Congress in 1946?
questions.solution: Jawaharlal Nehru served as the Vice President of the Executive Council in the Interim Government (formed Sept 1946). Note: The Viceroy (Lord Wavell, then Mountbatten) remained the President.

questions.question: Who among the following has written the biography of Buddha, Buddhacharita?
questions.solution: Buddhacharita, a masterpiece of Sanskrit literature on the life of Buddha, was written by Ashvaghosha. Patron: He was the spiritual advisor/poet in the court of Kushan King Kanishka.

questions.question: Who among the following designed a campaign that came to be known as the ‘Rowlatt Satyagraha’?
questions.solution: Mahatma Gandhi organized the Rowlatt Satyagraha in 1919 against the 'Black Act' (Rowlatt Act) which allowed detention without trial. Outcome: This led to the Jallianwala Bagh Massacre (April 13, 1919).

questions.question: The Lucknow Pact was signed in ______ by Congress and the Muslim League to work in alliance for representative government.
questions.solution:
The Lucknow Pact (1916) was a joint session of the INC and Muslim League. Key points:
  • United the Moderates and Extremists of the Congress.
  • Congress accepted the Separate Electors for Muslims.
  • Bal Gangadhar Tilak and M.A. Jinnah played key roles.

questions.question: Who among the following was NOT associated with ‘Prarthana Sabha’?
questions.solution: Prarthana Samaj was founded in 1867 by Atmaram Pandurang. Prominent members: R.G. Bhandarkar and M.G. Ranade. Motilal Nehru was not associated with it (he was a prominent Congress leader and lawyer).

questions.question: Who among the following Bahmani sultans transferred his capital from Gulbarga to Bidar?
questions.solution: Ahmad Shah I (r. 1422–1436) shifted the capital of the Bahmani Sultanate from Gulbarga to Bidar. Reason: Strategy and climate. He is also known for building the Bidar Fort.

questions.question: Which of the following is the autobiography of the first Indian President Dr. Rajendra Prasad?
questions.solution: Atmakatha (meaning 'Autobiography') is the life story written by Dr. Rajendra Prasad, the first President of India. Fact: He was the president of the Constituent Assembly.

questions.question: The office of Diwan-i-Insha dealt with which affair in administration?
questions.solution: The Diwan-i-Insha was the department of Royal Correspondence during the Delhi Sultanate. Head: Dabir-i-Mamalik. It managed all formal communications between the Sultan and local governors.

questions.question: When was the National Interim Government of India formed, under Jawaharlal Nehru?
questions.solution: The Interim Government of India was formed on 2 September 1946. Purpose: To assist the transition of India from British rule to independence. It remained in place until August 15, 1947.

questions.question: Which of the following Sultans of Delhi was appointed as Amir-i-Tuzuk (Master of Ceremonies) before becoming the Sultan?
questions.solution: Alauddin Khalji served as the Amir-i-Tuzuk (Master of Ceremonies) during the reign of his uncle/predecessor Jalaluddin Khalji. Fact: He later introduced the Market Control Policy and the Dagh (branding of horses) system.

questions.question: Who among the following classical poets of the Sultanate period in India popularised Qawwali, a form of music which derived its name from the Arabic word ‘qaul’, meaning ‘to speak’?
questions.solution: Amir Khusrau (1253–1325), known as the 'Parrot of India' (Tuti-e-Hind), popularized Qawwali. Instruments: He is often credited with inventing the Sitar and the Tabla.

questions.question: Which of the following is an autobiography of a Bengali illiterate woman who secretly acquired literacy skills to read sacred texts in an age when girls and women were denied education and deemed fit only for household chores?
questions.solution: Amar Jiban (published in 1876) is the first autobiography written by an Indian woman, Rassundari Devi. Significance: She secretly learned to read and write by scratching letters on the kitchen wall while performing domestic chores.

questions.question: When was the Atmiya Sabha founded to attack the evils within Hinduism?
questions.solution: Atmiya Sabha (Society of Friends) was founded by Raja Ram Mohan Roy in 1814 (Calcutta). Purpose: To conduct religious debates and promote monotheism while campaigning against social evils like Sati.

questions.question: Who succeeded Alivardi Khan as Nawab of Bengal?
questions.solution: Siraj-ud-Daulah succeeded his grandfather Alivardi Khan as the Nawab of Bengal in 1756. History: He was later defeated by the British in the Battle of Plassey (1757).

questions.question: Who among the following founded an expatriate Communist Party of India at Tashkent in 1920?
questions.solution: M.N. Roy founded the Communist Party of India (CPI) in Tashkent (now in Uzbekistan) in October 1920. Fact: He was a pioneer of the Radical Humanist movement.

questions.question: Europeans entered India with a mindset of trading only. This streak was initiated by which of the following European nations?
questions.solution: The Portuguese were the first Europeans to reach India for trade via the sea route (Vasco da Gama in 1498). Timeline of Arrivals: Portuguese → Dutch → British → Danish → French.

questions.question: In which year Timur’s invasion of Delhi took place?
questions.solution: Timur invaded India in 1398. Aftermath: He appointed Khizr Khan as his deputy in India, who eventually founded the Sayyid Dynasty in 1414.
